name: Temporal rotation flap

card.summary: A reconstructive surgical technique that rotates a flap of temple skin into a nearby defect or to preserve the hairline, discussed in hairline and facial work for natural-looking results.
card.note: Surgical procedure with risks of flap loss, scarring and hair displacement; published use is mainly reconstructive.

quick.overview:
A temporal rotation flap moves a piece of skin from the temple area, still attached to its blood supply, by rotating it to cover a defect or to hold the hairline in place. In hairline and face-lift discussions it comes up as a way to keep the hairline at the temples looking natural.

The published literature is surgical case series: eyelid and ear reconstruction, and a French paper on preserving the hairline in cervicofacial lifts.
quick.how: It is performed by a surgeon, typically under local or general anesthesia, as part of a larger reconstruction or face-lift. It is not a home or non-surgical method.
quick.risks: As with other flaps, risks include poor flap survival, scarring, hair displacement and infection; the published series report few complications in selected patients.

lead: A temporal rotation flap is a surgical technique in which skin from the temple is rotated on a pedicle to cover a nearby defect or to reposition tissue. In looksmaxxing discussions of hardmaxxing it is mentioned in connection with hairline work. [1][4]

In published surgery, French plastic surgeons described a double temporal and retroauricular rotation flap to limit hair displacement after cervicofacial lifts, resecting a de-epithelialized triangle and using an L flap behind the ear to reconstruct hairline continuity. [4] Other reports use the flap for reconstruction: lower-eyelid defects combined with an acellular dermal graft, and cryptotia correction. [1][2]

chain: Temple skin is rotated on its blood supply
Hairline continuity or a defect is reconstructed
angle.text: In face-lift work, the flap is used to keep the sideburn and temple hairline from rising, which keeps the face looking natural after surgery. In reconstruction it matches skin color and texture.

infobox: Hairline preservation, eyelid and ear reconstruction

paras: The flap remains attached at its base and is turned into the defect. Variants combine it with cartilage plasty or grafts. [1][2]

Hairline preservation: a 1992 paper details a double temporal and retroauricular rotation flap in facelifts. [4] Eyelid reconstruction: six patients had full-thickness lower-eyelid defects repaired with 100% flap survival at six months and matching color and texture. [1] Ear reconstruction: eight cases of cryptotia (ten ears) corrected with stable results and inconspicuous scars. [2]

The studies are small surgical series. The eyelid series (six patients) reported no pain or corneal irritation and inconspicuous donor scars. [1] The cryptotia series (eight patients, follow-up 3 months to 1 year) reported no hematoma, infection or flap necrosis. [2] The 1992 hairline paper is a technique description. [4]

timeline.event: Technique for hairline preservation in facelifts described. [4]
